knight_criteria.rationale: The story materially engages speculative science: spectroscopic analysis showing bands unlike any known spectrum, talk of new elements, silicon affinity, and characterization of the entity as a gas obeying laws not of our cosmos. Scientific facts and speculative science are central to the narrative.

No engineered device, technique, or invention materially affects the setting, problem, or outcome. Laboratory instruments (spectroscope, reagents) are ordinary tools of investigation rather than a plot-driving invention; the reservoir is incidental framing. The driving force is an alien natural phenomenon, not technology.

The story is set in a near-past frame ('forty-four years ago', the 1880s) told to a contemporary surveyor, and features spatial displacement of an entity arriving from and departing to interstellar space. This is arrival/departure across cosmic distance rather than a strongly speculative future or remote past or genuine time travel, so materiality and interpretation are uncertain.

The narrative systematically develops consequences from the premise of an extraterrestrial substance: progressive corruption of crops, vegetation, livestock, humans, and land, and the ongoing spreading blight. This methodical extrapolation of effects from an identifiable premise is central.

The professors observe, sample, and systematically test the meteorite with reagents, acids, crucible, spectroscope, and later analyze dust samples linking their spectrum to the meteor. This observation, measurement, and systematic inference materially drive understanding, even though it ultimately fails.

The meteorite and its color are explicitly extra-cosmic visitors from 'realms of infinity beyond all Nature,' obeying laws not of our cosmos and departing back into space. A visitor from a nonordinary cosmic environment is central to the story.

The color's presence causes a large-scale biological and environmental catastrophe: the destruction of an entire family and farm, the eruptive cataclysm, five acres of dead grey desert, and an ongoing spreading blight. This disaster is actual and causally central.
